title: Quantum Indeterminacy
definition: The phenomenon in quantum mechanics where a particle's state is not definitively known until it is observed or measured.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a quantum particle as being in a state of both possibilities at once, until we look at it and decide which one it is.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Quantum indeterminacy is a consequence of the wave-particle duality in quantum mechanics. It challenges the classical notion of determinism and highlights the probabilistic nature of quantum systems.
difficulty_levels.expert: Quantum indeterminacy raises profound philosophical questions about the nature of reality and the role of observation in shaping it. It also has connections to information theory and the concept of entropy, and has been used to explore fundamental questions in quantum foundations and the nature of measurement.

extra_fields.insight: Quantum indeterminacy highlights the inherent uncertainty in the quantum world and challenges classical notions of determinism.
